chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:
If a man forcibly takes possession of a female slave and then claims/demands her, he is liable for one-tenth of her value; and if she is a free woman, he is liable for the dowry.

key_terms.اقْتَضَّهَا: He claimed/demanded her (in a legal context)
key_terms.اِغْتَصَبَ: To forcibly take possession or seize

ai.seo_question: What is the financial compensation for forcibly taking a female slave versus a free woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes a distinct legal precedent in Shia jurisprudence regarding the financial liability for a man who forcibly takes possession of a female, differentiating between slaves and free women. For a slave, the penalty is set at one-tenth (ushr) of her market value, reflecting the specific rules of *ghasb* (usurpation) applied to chattel, whereas for a free woman, the liability is the full dowry (sadaq), emphasizing her status and the sanctity of her marital rights. This distinction highlights the nuanced approach of the Imams in assigning compensation based on social and legal status.
